name: Sharetribe
title: Sharetribe SvelteKit Storefront — Svelte Commerce Connector
description: Svelte Commerce on Sharetribe: 21 of 43 services wired. A marketplace, not a webshop: listings map to products, but the storefront cannot buy through it yet.
lede: Sharetribe is a marketplace, not a webshop, so the connector maps a listing to a product and a transaction to an order. There is deliberately no cart, no coupon and no category tree, and the storefront’s buying path is inert.
verdict: Listings, sign-in and orders are wired, but the storefront cannot buy through it yet. Sharetribe has no cart and no checkout: buying is a transaction on one listing, moved through the marketplace’s own process, with money moving only through Stripe Connect. The connector ships Sharetribe-native transaction commands; the storefront’s cart and payment step do not use them, and its gateway methods throw `NotSupportedError`.

quickStart.text: one connector at a time: remove the two the storefront ships with, add this one
point it at your Sharetribe marketplace

env.name: PUBLIC_SHARETRIBE_API_URL
env.note: Base URL of the Marketplace API. Boot fails, naming this variable, if it is missing.

env.name: PUBLIC_SHARETRIBE_CLIENT_ID
env.note: The Marketplace API application’s client ID — the OAuth2 `client_id`, and the path segment the Asset Delivery API authenticates with. `PUBLIC_SHARETRIBE_API_KEY` is read in its place if it is unset.

env.name: PUBLIC_SHARETRIBE_API_KEY
env.note: Accepted as the client ID when `PUBLIC_SHARETRIBE_CLIENT_ID` is unset.

env.name: PUBLIC_SHARETRIBE_API_SECRET
env.note: The client secret. See the limitations before setting it.

env.name: PUBLIC_SHARETRIBE_ACCESS_TOKEN
env.note: A user access token, sent as a bearer token. Every transaction call needs one.

env.name: PUBLIC_SHARETRIBE_ASSET_URL
env.note: The Asset Delivery API host, if it must be overridden. Defaults to `https://cdn.st-api.com`, a different host from the Marketplace API.

env.name: PUBLIC_CONNECTOR
env.note: Only when more than one connector is installed: `@misiki/sharetribe-connector` names the one this build runs on.

envNote: `init.ts` hands the connector every `PUBLIC_SHARETRIBE_*` variable that is set, camel-cased. The guide also lists `PUBLIC_SHARETRIBE_ACCESS_KEY`, `PUBLIC_SHARETRIBE_STORE_ID` and `PUBLIC_SHARETRIBE_CHANNEL_ID`; the connector’s source does not read them.
backendSettings: Create a Marketplace API application in Sharetribe; its client ID goes in `PUBLIC_SHARETRIBE_CLIENT_ID`.
howItWorks: The connector maps Sharetribe’s model onto the storefront’s: a listing becomes a product, a transaction becomes an order. It also reads Sharetribe’s Asset Delivery API, which lives on a different host from the Marketplace API.

Buying on Sharetribe is initiating a transaction on one listing and moving it through the marketplace’s own transaction process, whose aliases and transitions are specific to each marketplace. The connector ships commands for that; it does not guess the process names, because a wrong guess fails. The storefront’s cart and per-gateway checkout have no Sharetribe equivalent, so they throw rather than return a fake receipt.
limitations: The storefront cannot complete a purchase. Its payment step calls one method per gateway, keyed by a cart; Sharetribe has neither, and money moves only through Stripe Connect inside a transaction. Each gateway method throws `NotSupportedError`, and the connector’s Sharetribe-native transaction commands are not called by the storefront yet.
Cart: not wired — deliberately: Sharetribe has no cart, so the storefront’s cart is inert.
Coupons: not wired — deliberately: Sharetribe has no coupons.
If you set `PUBLIC_SHARETRIBE_API_SECRET`, the client secret reaches every visitor: SvelteKit sends `PUBLIC_` variables to the browser.

faq.q: Can I run a Sharetribe marketplace on Svelte Commerce today?
faq.a: Not to take bookings or sales. Listings, sign-in and orders are wired, but Sharetribe has no cart and no checkout, and the storefront’s buying path expects both. The connector has Sharetribe-native transaction commands; the storefront does not call them yet.

faq.q: How do I switch Svelte Commerce to Sharetribe?
faq.a: Remove the connectors the storefront ships with, install `@misiki/sharetribe-connector`, set `PUBLIC_SHARETRIBE_API_URL` in `.env` and start the dev server. `vite.config.ts` resolves whichever connector is installed, so no file in the storefront changes.

faq.q: Why is there no cart on Sharetribe?
faq.a: Because Sharetribe does not have one. Buying is a transaction on a single listing, moved through the marketplace’s own process. The connector maps listings to products and transactions to orders, and leaves the cart and coupons deliberately empty. Its authors have asked Sharetribe’s maintainers whether that mapping is the one they would recommend.

openQuestion: Is `listing` to `Product` the mapping you would recommend, or should a storefront model transactions as the primary entity?

api.surface: The connector calls three Sharetribe surfaces: the Marketplace API under `/v1/api` for every resource route, the Authentication API under `/v1/auth` for `/token` and `/revoke` only, and the Asset Delivery API under `/v1/assets/pub/<client id>` on a separate host for Console-managed content.
api.auth: Every Marketplace API call carries `Authorization: bearer <access_token>`, because Sharetribe has no unauthenticated mode; before the first call the connector posts a form-encoded `client_credentials` grant with `scope=public-read` to `/v1/auth/token`, a shopper signs in with the `password` grant and `scope=user`, and the tokens are kept in the connector’s in-memory credentials, not in a cookie.

calls.what: `GET <asset host>/v1/assets/pub/<client id>/a/latest/listings/listing-categories.json` for the tree; products by `pub_categoryLevel1` on `/listings/query`
`POST /v1/auth/token` (password grant), then `GET /v1/api/current_user/show`; `POST /v1/api/current_user/create` to register; `POST /v1/auth/revoke` to sign out

rules: The connector sets `Accept: application/json` last on every request, because without it Sharetribe answers in Transit, where ids and prices are typed objects that nothing in the connector decodes.

Sharetribe’s sort convention is the reverse of the storefront’s: a bare attribute sorts descending and a `-` makes it ascending, so the storefront’s `-createdAt` is sent as `createdAt`, and with a keyword search the default sort is dropped so results stay in relevance order.

Prices are integers in the currency’s minor unit, so `1590` in USD is shown as 15.90, a price-range filter is converted to minor units before it is sent, and zero-decimal and three-decimal currencies are handled separately.
Writes go through `?expand=true`, because a Sharetribe command otherwise returns only a bare `{ id, type }` reference.

Token requests are single-flight so a burst of parallel calls fetches one token, and a 429 is retried up to three times, honouring `Retry-After`, because development marketplaces allow 1 GET per second and 1 POST per 2 seconds per IP.
